note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-23): 14 pictures from 28 trial pictures. Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. Since the word box (2026-11-23), the important part of every picture sits in the upper half to 60% of the frame or out at the sides, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job and his friends are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown. Picture ideas already used in Job 18-20 were avoided.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures.

sections.meaning: Job asks his friends to stop answering and simply listen, because what he is about to say appalls even him and should shock them into silence.
ideas: On a back porch a worn grey-haired man speaks quietly while three friends sit before him in silence; one has pressed his hand over his mouth, eyes wide in shock
A worn man raises one open hand for silence at a table where three men had been talking over each other, and they fall quiet
Close view of a man's face, hand clapped over his mouth, eyes wide, listening to something terrible
A man sits alone at night on the edge of his bed, arms wrapped round himself, shuddering as he remembers
A friend sits beside a grieving man on a bench, simply listening, saying nothing
A man holding a finger to his lips to ask for quiet
Three men frozen mid-gesture, mouths shut, as a worn man begins to speak
An old man's hand trembling on the arm of a chair, gooseflesh on his arm
A cup of tea going cold untouched between silent listeners
A worn man shows his thin, scarred arms as his friends stare

sections.meaning: The wicked are not cut down young: they live to old age, grow rich and powerful, see their children's children round them, and live in safe homes that no punishment from God touches.
ideas: A hale silver-haired rich man sits at ease on the terrace of a grand house, glass in hand, smiling down at his grown children and many grandchildren playing on the sunny lawn
A family photograph being taken on the wide steps of a mansion: a proud, robust old man in the middle, rows of children and grandchildren round him
A grand house at dusk with every window glowing warmly and its gates standing open, untroubled
An old rich man laughing on the deck of his yacht in calm blue water, surrounded by family
A sturdy grandfather lifting a laughing grandchild high on the lawn of an estate
A walled estate in sunshine, the gate unguarded, a dog asleep on the warm doorstep
An old man in perfect health striding up a hill ahead of his grandsons
A rich old man asleep in a hammock in his garden, untroubled
A great old oak shading a big house, a large family picnicking beneath it
A white-haired man at a long birthday table surrounded by four generations

sections.meaning: Everything they have flourishes: their herds multiply, their children dance to music, they spend their days in good things, and when death comes it is quick and easy.
ideas: In a lush green pasture a big strong bull stands beside a cow licking her healthy newborn calf
A wide valley of fat cattle grazing in golden afternoon light, calves among them, as far as the eye can see
On a sunlit lawn at a garden party a ring of young children dance hand in hand while a small band plays drum, guitar and flute beside them
A crowd of small children run out through an open farm gate across a meadow like a flock of lambs, while a man plays a flute by the gate
A long table under strings of lights, grown-ups laughing, music playing
A barn full of healthy newborn calves
A grandfather dancing with his granddaughter at a wedding
An old man dozing peacefully in a garden chair at sunset after the party
A flute player and a drummer on a porch, children clapping
Lambs and children running together down a green hillside

sections.meaning: Those who live this well tell God to leave them alone and see no gain in serving him or praying to him, though their good was never in their own hands; Job wants nothing to do with their way of thinking.
ideas: In a luxurious penthouse a man in a silk robe pulls the heavy curtains shut against a flood of bright morning light, turning his back on it
Rich friends laughing over drinks on a terrace, all with their backs turned to a glorious sunrise
A worn grey-haired man in a plain jacket turns and walks away from a table where well-dressed men lean together over papers, scheming
A worn man turns his back on a lavish party in a lit mansion and walks away down the dark drive
A man in a suit shuts a door while bright light streams through the gap
A man tossing an unopened letter into the bin
A man at a desk with a calculator, shaking his head, asking what is in it for him
A rich man counting money with his back to an open window full of light
An empty open palm held up beside a mansion
A man switching off a lamp so he can sleep in the dark

sections.meaning: Job challenges what the friends claim: how often does the wicked man's lamp really go out, or does he really blow away like chaff? Seldom.
ideas: At night in a storm an oil lamp burns tall and steady in the window of a grand house while the wind bends the trees outside
A great mansion on a hill at night in a gale, every window still blazing with warm light
A candle in a glass lantern on a porch that does not flicker though leaves whirl past
A heap of straw that the wind does not move while a dust devil passes by
A row of street lamps shining on through a storm
A rich man's lit windows reflected in calm water while storm clouds pass harmlessly
Chaff blown off a field by a whirlwind
A golden stack of hay standing untouched after a storm
A man with a lantern walking safely through a storm
A lamp left burning all night in a quiet rich house

sections.meaning: The friends say God saves a man's punishment for his children, but a dead man does not care what happens to his house after him: let the wicked man pay himself and see it with his own eyes.
ideas: In a lawyer's office two grown sons sit stunned before a desk piled with stacks of their late father's debts, while above them a large oil portrait of the father smiles contentedly
In a fine restaurant a well-fed older man strolls out the door, smiling and unconcerned, while at the table his young son stares in dismay at the bill the waiter has just put down
A rich old man smiling as he sails away on a cruise ship while his sons on the dock hold a pile of bills
Sons standing in an empty repossessed house under their father's portrait
A young man carrying a heavy sack on his back that his father packed
An old man in a mirror seeing his own downfall
A boy sweeping up the mess after his father's party
An hourglass running out on a desk
A son paying at a counter while his father walks away
A grandson working a field of stones his grandfather ruined

sections.meaning: No one can teach God, yet death treats all alike: one man dies well fed and at ease, another dies bitter, never having had any good, and both lie together in the dust.
ideas: In one hospital room two old men lie in beds side by side: one plump and content among flowers and fruit, the other gaunt and bitter under a thin blanket, nothing on his table
Two old men on one park bench: one plump and content in a good coat, the other thin and bitter in a threadbare coat
Two graves side by side in one patch of earth: a grand polished granite headstone heaped with fresh flowers beside a bare mound with a small plain wooden stake
Two graves side by side, one with a tall grand monument and one with a small plain stone, both covered alike by the same drift of fallen leaves
Two pairs of shoes left side by side at a grave: polished leather and worn-out boots
A rich man's coffin and a poor man's plain box side by side
A golden leaf and a brown leaf lying together on the ground
A chess king and a pawn put away in the same box
A lavish dinner plate and an empty tin bowl side by side on the bare earth
A cemetery where a grand tomb and a pauper's plot share the same soil

sections.meaning: Job sees what his friends are really saying: when they ask where the wicked man's house has gone, they mean his own ruined house.
ideas: Three men in good coats lean together whispering behind their hands, glancing at a worn grey-haired man on an upturned crate nearby, who has turned and looks straight at them, knowing
Three men in good coats stand on the bare foundation where a house once stood, one spreading his open hands as if asking where it went, while a worn man watches them from the side
A worn man looking through a window at friends conferring outside
A man catching his friends exchanging knowing looks
Three men looking down at an empty plot where a tent once stood
A worn man reading the faces of his friends across a table
Friends passing notes behind a man's back
Three men pointing at an empty lot next to a ruin
A man looking at his own reflection in a broken window while friends talk
A worn man nodding slowly as his friends' meaning dawns on him

sections.meaning: Anyone who has travelled knows the truth: the evil man escapes disaster, no one dares confront him or repay him, and he is buried with honour, followed by crowds.
ideas: A rich man in a suit calmly steps into a private helicopter on a rooftop while far below the city streets lie flooded
A powerful man in a dark suit walks down a long hall between two lines of people who lower their eyes; no one dares look at him
A huge funeral: a hearse heaped with flowers leads a long line of black cars and hundreds of mourners along a tree-lined avenue, stretching back out of sight
A grand marble tomb on a green hill with two uniformed guards standing watch at its door, flowers piled before it
A rich man in sunglasses on his yacht far out in calm water while a storm lashes the coast behind him
A man in a suit walking out of a courthouse smiling, free
A long line of people filing past a flower-covered coffin in a grand hall
An old hiker at a crossroads pointing back down the road, telling a younger traveller
A wealthy man stepping from a limousine as people step aside
Travellers at a roadside cafe telling the locals what they have seen

sections.meaning: The friends' comfort is empty breath, and all that is left of their answers is falseness.
ideas: One of three friends holds out a cup to a worn grey-haired man sitting on the ground; the cup is plainly empty, and the man looks into it
A friend hands a worn man a beautifully wrapped gift box; he has opened it and it is empty
The worn man rises and walks away from his three seated friends toward open country
A friend's hand patting a man's shoulder while the man stares ahead unmoved
A jug tipped over a glass with nothing coming out
Breath vanishing on a cold window
An empty bowl handed to a hungry man
A hollow chocolate egg broken open to nothing
A bandage stuck on the wrong arm
Soap bubbles blown toward a weeping man

scenes.principle: Hear my word carefully, and let this be your comforts. Turn to me and be appalled, and put your hand on your mouth.
scenes.shows: On a back porch a worn grey-haired man speaks quietly while three friends sit silent before him; one has pressed his hand over his mouth in shock.
scenes.prompt: On the wooden back porch of a plain house in grey afternoon light, a worn, thin, grey-haired man sits on a low stool, speaking quietly and earnestly. Facing him, three middle-aged men in good coats sit on a bench in stunned silence; the nearest has pressed his hand over his mouth, his eyes wide with shock, and the others sit very still. All four faces and the hand over the mouth are high in the frame. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Why do the wicked live, grow old, and even grow mighty in wealth? Their offspring are established before them.
scenes.shows: A hale silver-haired rich man sits at ease on the terrace of a grand house, glass in hand, smiling down at his grown children and many grandchildren on the sunny lawn.
scenes.prompt: On the stone terrace of a grand country house on a bright summer afternoon, a hale, broad, silver-haired old man in an expensive sweater sits at ease in a cushioned chair, a glass in his hand, smiling with satisfaction as he looks down over his estate, where his grown sons and daughters and many grandchildren play and talk on the wide sunny lawn. The old man and his family are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: His bull breeds and does not fail; his cow calves and does not miscarry.
scenes.shows: In a lush green pasture a big strong bull stands beside a cow licking her healthy newborn calf.
scenes.prompt: In a lush green pasture in soft morning light, a big, strong, glossy bull stands beside a healthy cow who is licking her newborn calf, already standing on wobbly legs; behind them more fat cattle graze on rolling green hills. The bull, the cow and the calf are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: They send out their young children like a flock, and their children dance. They lift their voice to the drum and lyre, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
scenes.shows: On a sunlit lawn at a garden party a ring of young children dance hand in hand while a small band plays drum, guitar and flute beside them.
scenes.prompt: On the sunlit lawn of a big garden party, a ring of young children in bright summer clothes dance hand in hand, laughing and skipping, while beside them a small band of three grown-ups plays a hand drum, an acoustic guitar and a wooden flute. The dancing children and the musicians are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And they say to God, 'Depart from us; we do not wish for the knowledge of your ways. What is the Almighty, that we should serve him?'
scenes.shows: In a luxurious penthouse a man in a silk robe pulls the heavy curtains shut against a flood of bright morning light, turning his face away from it.
scenes.prompt: In a luxurious penthouse bedroom, a well-fed man in a silk dressing gown stands at a tall window and pulls the heavy velvet curtains shut against a flood of brilliant morning light pouring in, turning his face away from the light with a scowl. The man, the curtains and the streaming light are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Look, their good is not in their hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
scenes.shows: A worn grey-haired man in a plain jacket turns and walks away from a table where well-dressed men lean together over papers, scheming.
scenes.prompt: In a rich wood-panelled room, four well-dressed men lean together over papers spread on a polished table, scheming in low voices; on the right side of the frame a worn, thin, grey-haired man in a plain jacket has turned his back on them and is walking out through the open door. The scheming men and the man leaving are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: How often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out, and their calamity comes upon them?
scenes.shows: At night in a storm an oil lamp burns tall and steady in the window of a grand house while the wind bends the trees outside.
scenes.prompt: At night in a wild storm, seen from outside, an oil lamp with a tall steady flame burns calmly in the window of a grand stone house, its warm glow unshaken, while the gale bends the trees and whips leaves and straw past the glass. The window and the lamp are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: 'God hides away his harm for his sons.' Let him repay it to him, so that he may know it. For what does he care about his house after him?
scenes.shows: In a lawyer's office two grown sons sit stunned before a desk piled with their late father's debts, while above them an oil portrait of the father smiles contentedly.
scenes.prompt: In a lawyer's office, two grown sons in dark clothes sit stunned before a desk piled high with folders and stacks of papers, their late father's debts, one son with his head in his hands; on the wall above them hangs a large oil portrait of their father, a rich, well-fed man smiling contentedly. The portrait and the sons' faces are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: One dies in his full strength, wholly untroubled and at ease. And another dies with a bitter soul, and has not eaten of the good.
scenes.shows: In one hospital room two old men lie in beds side by side: one plump and content among flowers and fruit, the other gaunt and bitter under a thin blanket.
scenes.prompt: In a hospital room two old men lie in beds side by side. On the left a plump, rosy, contented old man in silk pyjamas rests at ease against fat pillows, his bedside table crowded with flowers, fruit and chocolates. On the right a gaunt, hollow-cheeked old man lies bitter and staring under a thin grey blanket, his bedside table bare. Both men are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Together they lie down on the dust, and maggots cover them.
scenes.shows: Two graves side by side in one patch of earth: a grand polished headstone heaped with flowers beside a bare mound with a small plain wooden stake.
scenes.prompt: In a quiet country graveyard under a grey sky, two fresh graves lie side by side in the same bare earth: one with a grand polished granite headstone heaped with fresh flowers, the other only a bare mound of soil with a small plain wooden stake at its head. Both graves are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: Look, I know your plans, and the schemes with which you do violence to me.
scenes.shows: Three men in good coats whisper behind their hands, glancing at a worn grey-haired man nearby, who has turned and looks straight at them, knowing.
scenes.prompt: In a bare yard on a grey day, three middle-aged men in good coats stand close together on the left, whispering behind their hands and glancing sideways; on the right a worn, thin, grey-haired man sitting on an upturned wooden crate has turned his head and looks straight at them, calm and knowing. All four faces are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: That the evil man is spared in the day of calamity. Who tells him his way to his face? And what he has done, who repays him for it?
scenes.shows: A rich man in a suit calmly steps into a private helicopter on a rooftop while far below the city streets lie flooded.
scenes.prompt: On the rooftop helipad of a tall tower, a rich man in an expensive suit calmly steps up into a gleaming private helicopter, its door held open for him, unhurried and dry; far below, the city streets have become brown floodwater up to the windows of the cars. The man and the helicopter are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And he is carried to the graves, and watch is kept over the mound. Every human being follows after him, and those before him are without number.
scenes.shows: A huge funeral: a hearse heaped with flowers leads a long line of black cars and hundreds of mourners along a tree-lined avenue, stretching back out of sight.
scenes.prompt: Seen from above and ahead, a huge, stately funeral procession moves slowly along a wide tree-lined avenue: a black hearse heaped with white flowers in front, followed by a long line of black cars and hundreds of mourners in dark clothes on foot, the line stretching back out of sight. The hearse and the long procession fill the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.

scenes.principle: And how can you comfort me in vain? As for your replies, what is left is unfaithfulness.
scenes.shows: A friend hands a worn man a beautifully wrapped gift box; he has opened it and it is empty.
scenes.prompt: In a bare room, a worn, thin, grey-haired man sits holding a beautifully wrapped gift box with a ribbon, its lid lifted off; the box is plainly empty inside. Three men in good coats stand over him, smiling as if they have given him something. The worn man's weary face and the empty box are in the upper half of the picture. The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.
